questions.question: The genu of the internal capsule contains mainly the:
The anterior two-thirds of the posterior limb contains mainly:
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Corticospinal and extrapyramidal fibers

questions.question: The sensory radiation from the thalamus passes mainly through the which of the following part of the internal capsule?
options: Posterior half of the posterior limb
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Posterior half of the posterior limb

questions.question: A patient with an internal capsule lesion develops weakness of the opposite half of the body involving multiple muscle groups. Which type of paralysis is most likely present?
The typical paralysis associated with an internal capsule lesion is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Contralateral spastic hemiplegia

questions.question: Hypertonia in an internal capsule UMNL is partly explained by which of the following?
options: Increased activity of inhibitory medullary reticular formation
Intact facilitatory vestibular influence and reduced cortical inhibition of tone
Destruction of the anterior horn cells
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Intact facilitatory vestibular influence and reduced cortical inhibition of tone

questions.question: Which finding is characteristic of an established UMNL?
options: Loss of all superficial reflexes in every lesion
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Exaggerated tendon reflexes

questions.question: The plantar response in a typical UMNL may become?
options: A normal flexor response in all cases

questions.question: Muscle wasting is usually less marked in UMNL than LMNL due to which of the following?
options: The muscles no longer receive blood
The lower motor neuron and reflex muscle activation remain intact
The motor end plates disappear immediately
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. The lower motor neuron and reflex muscle activation remain intact

questions.question: Which finding best distinguishes LMNL from UMNL?
options: Flaccid paralysis with absent deep tendon reflexes
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Flaccid paralysis with absent deep tendon reflexes

questions.question: A patient with a lower motor neuron lesion is examined for deep and superficial reflexes. Which combination of findings is most likely?
options: Deep reflexes exaggerated, superficial reflexes absent
Deep reflexes intact, superficial reflexes exaggerated
Deep reflexes absent, superficial reflexes intact
Deep reflexes exaggerated, superficial reflexes intact
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Deep reflexes absent, superficial reflexes intact

questions.question: The characteristic type of hypertonia in spasticity is:
Which finding favors spasticity rather than rigidity?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: A. Babinski's sign and clonus

questions.question: Which feature is typical of LMNL?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: A. Marked muscle atrophy
